match.reason: The bank point covers Society and Culture methods such as interviews, focus groups and content analysis, not the experimental designs, correlational studies or controlled experiments the Psychology brief teaches, so no bank point teaches the same idea.

draft.title: Research methods
card: The researcher changes the independent variable and controls other factors. This is the method that can test cause and effect.
measures two variables to see if they are related. It does not change either one, so it cannot show that one causes the other.
A case study looks closely at one person, group or event. Fieldwork collects data in a real setting, such as a playground, without setting up the conditions.
Within-subjects: every participant does all conditions. Between-subjects: each participant does only one condition. Mixed: a design that uses both.
draft.remember: Match the method to the question: experiments test cause and effect, and the design sets who does which condition.

a.q: A researcher wants to test whether a new study app causes better test scores. Which method suits this question best?
opts: A case study of one student
a.why: Only a controlled experiment changes the independent variable and controls other factors, so it can test cause and effect. A correlational study is tempting, but it only shows whether two variables are related.
a.clue: Which method changes a variable on purpose?

b.q: Priya tests a reaction-time drink. Group A drinks it and Group B drinks water. Each person is tested once. Which design is this?
b.why: Each participant takes part in only one condition, so the design is between-subjects. It is not within-subjects, because that needs every participant to do both conditions.
